title: The Onion
text:
In The Brothers Karamazov, Grushenka tells Alyosha a folk tale she heard as a child from an old peasant woman.

Once there was a very wicked woman, and when she died she had not left behind a single good deed. The devils seized her and threw her into the lake of fire. Her guardian angel stood by, trying to think of some good thing she had done that he could tell to God. At last he remembered: once she had pulled an onion from her garden and given it to a beggar woman.

God told the angel to take that same onion, hold it out to her in the lake, and let her grab it. If he could pull her out by it, she could go to paradise. If the onion broke, she would stay where she was.

The angel held out the onion, and the woman seized it. He began to pull, carefully, and she was nearly out when the other sinners in the lake saw what was happening and grabbed onto her, hoping to be pulled out too. The woman kicked at them. "It is me being pulled out, not you! It is my onion, not yours!" As soon as she said that, the onion broke. She fell back into the lake, where she is burning to this day, and the angel wept and went away.
lesson: One small kindness can be a lifeline. Do not ruin what good you have by refusing to share it with others who are reaching for the same hope.
people: Grushenka, Alyosha, a wicked woman, her guardian angel
source: Fyodor Dostoevsky, The Brothers Karamazov (1880), Book VII, Chapter 3
